title: Braitenberg vehicles
why: A thought experiment: wire two sensors to two motors and the result seems to show fear, love or curiosity.

title: BEAM robots
why: Solar-powered bugs built from a handful of transistors, with no microcontroller and no code at all.

title: Off-grid mesh messaging
why: Meshtastic radios pass text messages for miles with no phone network or internet.
how: Read, then maybe buy a radio

title: Software-defined radio
why: A cheap USB stick lets you hear aircraft, weather satellites and much more.

title: Citizen air sensing
why: Thousands of people run home-built sensors that feed a live world map of air quality.

title: Shakey the robot
why: The first robot that could reason about its own actions, built in the 1960s. It wobbled.

title: Grey Walter's tortoises
why: Two valves and two sensors made 1940s robots that seemed to explore, hesitate and go home.

title: Passive walkers
why: Legged machines that stroll down a gentle slope with no motors, no sensors and no computer.

title: Soft robots
why: Robots made of rubber and air, with no rigid parts. Some are modelled on the octopus.

title: Swarm robotics
why: Hundreds of very simple robots that together form shapes none of them knows about.

title: Karakuri puppets
why: Clockwork dolls from Edo-period Japan that carry a cup of tea across the room to a guest.

title: The Jacquard loom
why: A loom controlled by punched cards, more than a century before computers borrowed the idea.

title: The uncanny valley
why: Why an almost-human robot is more unsettling than one that is plainly a machine.

title: RoboCup
why: A robot football league whose stated goal is to beat the human world champions by 2050.

title: Mars rovers
why: Robots driven from another planet, with a delay of minutes on every command.

title: The theremin
why: An electronic instrument from the 1920s that you play without touching it.

title: PID control
why: The century-old feedback idea behind cruise control, thermostats and balancing robots.

title: Slime mould that solves mazes
why: A single-celled blob with no brain that finds the shortest path between food sources.

title: High-altitude balloons
why: Hobbyists send cameras and sensors to the edge of space, then chase them down by radio.

title: Useless machines
why: A box whose only function is to switch itself off. One of the pioneers of AI built an early one.
